claim.why_it_matters: Four main entries are run together on one line, and from 'EVALUATE directive 52' through 'WRITE statement 233, 619' every line (main entries such as 'WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase', 'WITH LOCK phrase', 'Word 76' and their sub-entries alike) is flattened to one uniform 3-space indent, so the W-section index hierarchy is lost. verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 951 (printed 927) at 300 dpi. The PDF's W index section prints 'Weakly-typed items 132, 806', 'Week date format 630', 'Week-of-year subfield 630' and 'WHEN phrase' as four separate flush-left main entries, then two levels: main entries flush left (WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase, WHEN-COMPILED function 733, WITH DUPLICATES phrase, WITH LOCK phrase, ..., Word 76, Working-storage section 275, WRITE statement 233, 619) and indented sub-entries under them (EVALUATE directive 52, CLOSE statement 479, and so on). In page-951.md the first four are joined into one paragraph line, and every line from 'EVALUATE directive 52\' to 'WRITE statement 233, 619' carries the same 3-space indent, so main entries and sub-entries look identical. The Y and Z sections on the same page keep the hierarchy (with  ), which shows the W section has a transcription defect and not a style choice. No text is missing, but the parent of each sub-entry (for example, which phrase 'CLOSE statement 479' belongs to) can no longer be read reliably from the markdown. The claim quotes both sources accurately. It is a real defect, structural, and affects the index only (no normative content).
